quotes.speaker: SPEAKER

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Therefore Vice President Bush will get the first question.

quotes.quote: And I’m not sure, because of my concept of the vice presidency, that if I didn’t, I’d go doing what Mr.

quotes.quote: You can’t have the president of the United States out there looking over his shoulder wondering whether his vice president is going to be supporting him.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Two, I can walk into that Oval Office anytime and give him my judgment and he might agree or he might not.

quotes.quote: MASHEK: Congresswoman Ferraro, your opponent has served in the House Of Representatives, he’s been ambassador to the United Nations, ambassador to China, director of the Central Intelligence Agency and now he’s been vice president for four years.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I was a prosecutor for almost five years in the district attorney’s office in Queens County and I was a teacher.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: There’s not only what is on your paper resume that makes you qualified to run for or to hold office.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I, too, recall when Vice President Bush was running in the primary against President Reagan and he called the program voodoo economics, and it was and it is.

quotes.speaker: VANOCUR
quotes.quote: VANOCUR: Vice President Bush, you have one minute to rebuttal.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: With reference to civil rights I think you’ve got to go beyond that and if you take a look, also, at my record in the Congress and Fritz Mondale’s record, both in the Senate and as vice president, we both have extremely strong civil rights records.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: We’ve brought more civil rights cases in the Justice Department than the previous administration by far.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The interest rates when we left office were 21% percent.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I’m taking it from the historical viewpoint, if you go back to the 1600s when people came here, the reason they came to this country was to escape religious persecution, and that’s the same reason why people are coming here today in the 1940s to escape Nazism, now in the 1980s and 1984 when they can get our of the country to escape communism so they can come here and practice their religion.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Now what’s happened over the past several years, and quite frankly I’m not going to let you lay on me the intrusion of state politics into religion or religion into politics by my comments with reference to the president’s policies, because it started in 1980 when this administration was running for office and the Reverend Jerry Falwell became very, very involved in the campaign.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: If there comes a time where I cannot practice my religion and do my job properly, I will resign my job.

quotes.quote: FERRARO: Let me just say, first of all, that I almost resent, Vice President Bush, your patronizing attitude that you have to teach me about foreign policy.

quotes.speaker: QUARLES
quotes.quote: QUARLES: Vice President Bush, the last three Republican administrations, Eisenhower, Nixon, and Ford, none of them soft on communism, met with the Soviets and got agreements on arms control.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The president went, the first thing he did when he came into office was make a proposal on the most destabilizing weapons of all, START.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Chernenko, given more than a few months in office can solidify its position, then they’ll talk.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The last time I heard Vice President Bush blame the fact that they didn’t meet with the Soviet leader, and this is the first president in forty years not to meet with a Soviet counterpart.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Speaking of limits, I have to impose a limit on you, Vice President Bush?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: We now have 50,000 nuclear warheads; we are building at the rate of five or six a day between us and we have been doing that since this administration came into office.

quotes.quote: Vice President Monad has indicated that what he would do, first of all, as soon as he.

quotes.quote: Let me put it this way – I don’t have any questions, but we are so different from – the Reagan-Bush administration is so different from the Carter-Mondale [sic] administration that the American people are going to have the clearest choice.

quotes.speaker: BUSH
quotes.quote: BUSH: Well, in a couple of weeks, you, the American people, will be faced, three weeks, with a choice.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: It’s the clearest choice in some fifty years.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And the choice is, do we move forward with strength and with prosperity or do we go back to weakness, despair, disrespect.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: When Walter Mondale was attorney general of Minnesota, he led the fight for a man who could not afford to get justice because he couldn’t afford a lawyer; when he was in the Senate he fought for child nutrition programs, he wrote the Fair Housing Act, he even investigated the concerns and the abuses of migrant workers.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Children don’t vote and migrant workers exactly a powerful lobby in this country, but he did it because it was right.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Bruno introduces the vice presidential candidates and describes the format in his opening remarks.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: HAL BRUNO: Good evening from Atlanta and welcome to the vice presidential debate sponsored by the Nonpartisan Commission on Presidential Debates.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The participants are Republican Vice President Dan Quayle.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: (APPLAUSE) And retired Vice Admiral James Stockdale, who is the vice presidential nominee — (APPLAUSE) — for independent candidate Ross Perot.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President — Dan, if I may — it was 16 years ago that you and I went to the Congress on the very first day together.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: (APPLAUSE) Harry Truman — VICE PRESIDENT QUAYLE: Do you remember the last time someone compared themselves to Jack Kennedy?

quotes.speaker: GORE
quotes.quote: GORE: Harry Truman, it’s worth remembering, assumed the presidency when Franklin Roosevelt died here in Georgia — only one of many occasions when fate thrust a vice president into the Oval Office in a time of crisis.

quotes.speaker: BRUNO
quotes.quote: BRUNO: Okay, the next statement will be from Vice President Quayle.

quotes.speaker: QUAYLE
quotes.quote: QUAYLE: Well, thank you, Senator Gore, for reminding me about my performance in the 1988 vice presidential debate.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I thought since you’re running for vice president, that we ought to start off by talking about the vice presidency itself.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The vice president presides over the Senate, he casts a deciding vote in case of a tie, but his role really depends on the assignments that are given to him by the president.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: However, if a president should die in office, or is unable to serve for any other reason, the vice president automatically becomes president, and that has happened 5 times in this century.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: What role would each of you like to play as vice president, what areas interest you, and what are your qualifications to serve as president, if necessary?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: In the case of Vice President Quayle, who we’re starting with, I suppose you’d tell us the role that you did play in the first term and which you’d like to do in a 2nd term.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: But even as vice president you never know exactly what your role is going to be from time to time, and let me just give you an example of where I was tested under fire and in a crisis.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Discussions of the vice presidency tend sometimes to focus on the crisis during which a vice president is thrust into the Oval Office, and indeed, one-3rd of the vice presidents who have served have been moved into the White House.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Now I’d like to say in response to Vice President Quayle- -he talked about Malta and the Philippines.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: But when you’re president of the US or when you’re vice president and you have to fill in like I did the night of the crisis in the Philippines, you’ve got to make a decision, you’ve got to make up your mind.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President, let him say his thoughts, and then you can come in.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President Quayle and Senator Gore both served on the Senate Armed Services Committee.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The numbers, in terms of the dollar cuts, as they stand on our plans now, show us almost the same as the vice president’s.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: — Governor Clinton’s plan is almost twice as much a cut as either one of us.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: This wasn’t a partisan victory that came suddenly, a few months after you took the oath of office.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: It is not the issue of how he avoided military service 20-some years ago; it’s the fact — it’s the fact that he does not tell the truth about it.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: He first said he didn’t get an induction notice, then we find out that he did; he said he didn’t have an ROTC slot, then we find out he did; he said he didn’t use Senator Fulbright’s office for special influence, then we find out that he did.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And, Vice President Quayle, it’s your turn to start first.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: You don’t have to have a choice between the environment and jobs — you can have both.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: No, Hal, the choice isn’t the environment and jobs.

quotes.speaker: QUAYLE
quotes.quote: QUAYLE: Okay, well, we’ll find — BRUNO: Let him talk, Mr Vice President.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: There is no incentive for a doctor to curtail the expensive tests because he’s under threat of malpractice lawyers.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: You talk about increasing costs that the president has had on Capitol Hill- – medical malpractice reform legislation — for several years.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Wouldn’t that be nice to take $20.7 billion that we’re putting into our legal system and put it to preventive health care or women’s health care or something else besides trial lawyers?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: But no — you don’t want to reform the health care system to drive down costs through medical malpractice.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I also want to respond to the question about malpractice.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Do you know which state has the lowest malpractice premiums in the entire country?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Bill Clinton’s Arkansas does — partly because he has passed reform measures limiting the time during which malpractice suits can be filed.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: How can you talk about family values, Dan, and twice veto the Family Medical Leave Act?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Medical malpractice legislation has been before the Congress of the US and you tried to convince the American people that Bill Clinton is for tort reform?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: He writes Polly Williams, a Democrat state legislator in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, saying I’m for choice in education; then he goes to the NEA teachers union and says, sorry, I’m not for choice in education because you won’t let me be for choice in education.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The reason we are pro-choice and in favor of a woman’s right to privacy is because we believe that during the early stages of a pregnancy the government has no business coming in and ordering a woman to do what the government thinks is best.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: We ought to be able to build more common ground among those who describe themselves as pro-choice and pro-life in efforts to reduce the number of unwanted pregnancies.

quotes.speaker: BRUNO
quotes.quote: BRUNO: Vice President Quayle, your turn.

quotes.speaker: GORE
quotes.quote: GORE: Well, you notice in his response, that Dan did not say I support the right of a woman to choose.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Take the NAFTA agreement — GORE: Well, wait — BRUNO: Let’s stick with the question, Mr Vice President.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Mr Vice President, you’ll have a chance to — (APPLAUSE) You’ll have a chance in the closing statements.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: It’s becoming increasingly difficult to pay for public education, for transportation, for police and fire protection, the basic services that local government must provide.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President Quayle, it’s your turn to go first.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And I found out that when I really got down to putting out do’s and don’ts, and lots of these included take torture for this and that, and this and that, and never take any amnesty, for reasons they all understood and went along with.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President Quayle said they’re important, but George Bush eliminated them from his urban plan, and then — QUAYLE: Well, that’s not true.

quotes.speaker: GORE
quotes.quote: GORE: We support the public school choice to go to any public school of your choice.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Choice in education is a very important issue.

quotes.speaker: STOCKDALE
quotes.quote: STOCKDALE: I — I come down on the side of freedom of school choice.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Ultimately, it is a choice between hope and fear, a choice between the future and the past.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: (APPLAUSE.) BRUNO: Vice President Quayle.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And that’s why we support choice in education.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I was in Beaumont, Texas, and met with small business people, and they wanted to reform the civil justice system because they think our legal system costs too much and there’s too much of a delay in getting an answer.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Under President Bush’s health care reform package that woman won’t have to make a choice about going back to work or health care for her children, because she’ll have both.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: (APPLAUSE) BRUNO: That concludes this vice presidential debate.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I’d like to thank Vice President Quayle, Senator Gore, Admiral Stockdale for being participants.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Bush of Texas, and the Democratic candidate, Vice President Al Gore.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Good evening, Governor Bush, Vice President Gore.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: He’s a vice presidential nominee who represents — I think people got to see why I picked him.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: It means addressing the problems of injustice and inequity, along the lines of race and ethnicity here at home, because in all these other places around the world where they’re having these terrible problems, when they feel hope, it is often because they see in us a reflection of their potential.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President Gore, the governor mentioned the Middle East.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Like the vice president, I call on Chairman Arafat to have his people pull back to make the peace.

quotes.speaker: MODERATOR
quotes.quote: MODERATOR: So you don’t believe, Vice President Gore, that we should take sides and resolve this right now?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: When I was in the senate before I became vice president I was pushing for stronger action against Milosevic.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And as a result, our nation paid a price.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: But the reverse side of the question, Governor, that Vice President Gore mentioned, 600,000 people died in Rwanda in 1994.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And we’ve got to do a lot of work in Africa to promote democracy and trade, and there are some — Vice President mentioned Nigeria is a fledgling democracy.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And I think that’s where maybe the vice president and I begin to have some differences.

quotes.speaker: MODERATOR
quotes.quote: MODERATOR: Vice President Gore, do you agree with the governor’s views on nation building, the use of military, our military, for nation building as he described and defined it?

quotes.speaker: BUSH
quotes.quote: BUSH: First let me just say one comment about what the vice president said.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I’ve devoted in the budget I’ve proposed, as I said last week, more than twice as much as the governor has proposed.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: It’s an enormous problem and corruption in official agencies, like militaries and police departments around the world, customs officials, that’s one of the worst forms of it.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And we have a fundamental choice to make.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: So I’m not exactly sure where the vice president is coming from, but I think one way for us to end up being viewed as the ugly American is for us to go around the world saying, â€œwe do it this way, so should you.â€ Now, we trust freedom.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President, but I think the United States must be humble and must be proud and confident of our values, but humble in how we treat nations that are figuring out how to chart their own course.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: (LAUGHTER) MODERATOR: First, a couple of follow-ups from the vice presidential debate last week.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President Gore, would you support or sign, as president, a federal law banning racial profiling by police and other authorities at all levels of government?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: One of my concerns, though, is I don’t want to federalize the local police forces.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: But it’s very important that we not overstep our bounds and I think most people — most police officers are good, dedicated, honorable citizens who are doing their job, putting their lives at risk who aren’t bigoted or aren’t prejudiced.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And I also agree that most police officers, of course, are doing a good job and hate this practice also.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I talked to an African-American police officer in Springfield, Massachusetts not long ago who raised this question and said that in his opinion one of the biggest solutions is in the training.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And not only the training in police procedures, but human relations.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I think they’re different because they’re based on prejudice and hatred, which gives rise to crimes that have not just a single victim, but they’re intended to stigmatize and dehumanize a whole group of people.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: So racial profiling isn’t just an issue at local police forces.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And so to make sure we end up getting rid of basic structural prejudice is education.

quotes.speaker: MODERATOR
quotes.quote: MODERATOR: Vice President Gore, what would be on your racial discrimination elimination list as president?

quotes.speaker: GORE
quotes.quote: GORE: I’m talking about the one that was proposed to deal — BUSH: No — well, what the Vice President must not understand is we’ve got a hate crimes bill in Texas.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President, we’re happy with our laws on our books.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Another vice presidential debate follow-up.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I presume the Vice President supported it when the President signed that bill and supports it now.

quotes.speaker: MODERATOR
quotes.quote: MODERATOR: New subject, new question, Vice President Gore.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: I disagree with the vice president on this issue.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: What are they, Governor, from your point of view, between you and the Vice President?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: So in my state we toughen up the juvenile justice laws.

quotes.speaker: MODERATOR
quotes.quote: MODERATOR: Governor, did the — are the vice president’s figures correct about Texas?

quotes.speaker: MODERATOR
quotes.quote: MODERATOR: Let me put that directly to you, Vice President Gore.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And let me tell you exactly why I think that the choice he made to give a tax cut for the oil companies and others before addressing this — I mean, if you were the governor of a state that was dead last in health care for families, and all of a sudden you found yourself with the biggest surplus your state had ever had in its history, wouldn’t you want to maybe use some of it to climb from 50th to, say, 45 or 40 or something or maybe better?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President Gore, on the environment.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: There was a study just a few weeks ago suggesting that in summertime the north polar ice cap will be completely gone in 50 years.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: The book you mentioned that Vice President Gore wrote, he also called for taxing — big energy taxes in order to clean up the environment.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President, haven’t they been changing their opinion a little bit on global warming?

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: You, your running mate, your campaign officials have charged that Vice President Gore exaggerates, embellishes and stretches the facts, etcetera.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: Vice President, are now calling the governor a bumbler.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
quotes.quote: And Vice President Gore, you have two minutes.

quotes.speaker: SPEAKER
